findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow the expected rejection in the experiment oracle**

The Aughrim case is specifically meant to exercise the boundary-preserving rejection described earlier in this document: an undiscovered-secret claim is rejected, after which Phase B must still answer from permitted context. Requiring zero validation rejections makes that correct execution fail the objective oracle and allows the experiment to pass only by avoiding the behavior it is supposed to evaluate. Treat the expected secret-claim rejection as a fixture and score the response that follows it instead.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L134-L136](https://github.com/cgracia/rpgflow/blob/05af06407558d72e748587573b95c23050dadfc2/AGENTS.md#L134-L136)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Define the rejected-secret projection semantics**

This adopts a new Phase-B projection for rejected secret claims, while the current semantic model deliberately exposes only a generic `UNRESOLVED` marker and keeps hidden beliefs and fact links out of Phase B. Before this becomes the implementation contract, specify whether the signal is generic or identifies a fact/belief, who constructs it, its provenance, and what the narrator may expose; otherwise a future implementation can leak the existence or identity of an unrevealed secret through the new channel.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L81-L81](https://github.com/cgracia/rpgflow/blob/05af06407558d72e748587573b95c23050dadfc2/AGENTS.md#L81-L81)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Specify repeated samples for the frozen corpus**

The preceding #47 decision explicitly says the follow-up must use repetition because the original one-sample-per-case result could not distinguish sampling variance, but this experiment specification only enumerates four cases and gives no repetitions per case or aggregation rule. Running it as written could therefore reproduce the same inconclusive evidence while being presented as the required follow-up; pin the sample count, retry policy, and pass/fail aggregation before admission.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L136-L136](https://github.com/cgracia/rpgflow/blob/05af06407558d72e748587573b95c23050dadfc2/AGENTS.md#L136-L136)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Index the completed decision artifact**

This file is marked “Research & Decision Complete” and is referenced from `DECISIONS.md` as the durable detail record, but it is absent from `docs/documentation-map.md`. The map requires newly added durable documents to be classified there, so leaving this unindexed makes the adopted decision undiscoverable through the repository's documentation entry point.

  NPC still read as cryptic, which weighs on the referee-policy side. The RETAIN reasoning for
  #69 decision 3, and the "module authoring gap" attribution in DECISIONS.md, rest on a misreading.

  docs/validation/2026-09-26-fell-barrow-owner-session-review.md:66-68: T9–T10 = "secondary-entrance

  bargain stall, entrance rulings") and DECISIONS ("T9-T10 entrance ruling delay" cited as dialogue stall).
  The review does not attribute T9–T10 to an NPC conversation.

[F3] Engine/Projection "ownership" quietly makes open projection decisions.
  notes.md §3.2 assigns to Engine: "resolving the gap where negotiation_note was previously unprojected"
  and "Phase B receives a structured signal indicating that the secret is unrevealable".
  DECISIONS.md entry records "Engine/Projection owns surfacing offers/interaction notes ... and
  handling validation rejections" as an adopted split.
  - docs/hollow-bridge-authoring-notes.md:54-79 records negotiation_note non-projection as an OPEN
    choice ("chooses between projecting the fields into the NPC dossier and deleting them"); the
    Fell Barrow module comment (:496-500) says the referee deliberately never sees it.
  - Sending a validation-rejected claim signal into the Phase-B envelope is a projection change at the
    invariant-1 boundary (Phase B narrates from committed canon; rejected claims are not canon).

  decision is required ... stop"): these need a semantic-model statement or explicit framing as a
  candidate, not adoption as a layer-ownership decision.
